body:
This is an adversarial review generated by Grok Bot (an AI assistant) at Vince's request, checked against the code at `64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96`. Findings may contain mistakes; please verify.

**Summary.** The kernel-side change is correct and small: `verify_network_queue_rejections` now uses the same validator as device initialization, so a 1024-entry queue no longer trips the boot-time assertion. But it doesn't fix #4 end to end. `tests/qemu/boot.sh` still requires the serial log to say exactly `256`, so `make test` still fails on QEMU 10.0.13. The gate doc skipped a QEMU 10.0.13 run because "issue #4 identifies the assertion failure precisely". That run is exactly what would have caught the second assertion.

**What I ran** (x86-64 Linux VM, Rust 1.99.0 from `rust-toolchain.toml`, Debian QEMU 10.0.13, OVMF 2025.02, TCG because the VM has no KVM access):
- `make check` on this head passed.
- `make test` on #9's head without this PR fails with `ginux: virtio network initialization invariant failed`. That's #4 reproduced, and QEMU logs `receive queue size: 1024`.
- `make test` on #9 with this PR merged in: the kernel boots to `GINUX_KERNEL_OK`, then `boot.sh` fails with `the bounded virtio-net discovery boundary was not established` because of the `256` grep below.

Severity: **P0** critical correctness/security bug or a false claim, **P1** high (claim overstated in a way that matters, or the property isn't actually enforced), **P2** medium, **P3** low, **P4** minor, **P5** nit. "Overengineering risk" estimates how likely a fix is to grow into new machinery that isn't needed yet, and says what not to build.

### Findings

- [ ] **P1: `make test` still fails on QEMU 10.0.13, because `boot.sh` hardcodes 256 a second time**
  - Evidence: [`tests/qemu/boot.sh#L164-L165`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/tests/qemu/boot.sh#L164-L165) greps for `virtio-net receive/transmit queue size: 256`. With this PR merged, the kernel prints `1024` and passes its own check, and then the script fails. The gate's acceptance criterion ([`13-virtio-queue-size-compatibility.md#L39`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/hdae/gates-todo/13-virtio-queue-size-compatibility.md#L39)) is met inside the kernel, but #4's symptom (red `make test`) remains. The decision not to run QEMU 10.0.13 ([`#L60-L61`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/hdae/gates-todo/13-virtio-queue-size-compatibility.md#L60-L61)) is why this was missed.
  - Smallest fix: make those two greps accept any valid size, for example `grep -Eq '^ginux: virtio-net receive queue size: (8|16|32|64|128|256|512|1024|2048|4096|8192|16384|32768)[[:space:]]*$'`. Serial lines end in `\r`, so a bare `$` anchor won't match. I tried exactly this locally and the virtio-net discovery block then passes on QEMU 10.0.13.
  - Overengineering risk: **Low.** It's a two-line test change. Don't add a QEMU version matrix to CI for this. One run on the QEMU version from #4 is enough evidence.

- [ ] **P4: the boot-time check is now weaker, and nothing outside the kernel pins the host-reported geometry**
  - Evidence: before, the check proved QEMU offered exactly 256/256. Now any power of two ≥ 8 passes ([`pci.rs#L3442-L3446`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/pci.rs#L3442-L3446)). That's the intended behavior, and the driver still programs its own 8-entry queues. I'm only noting that the extra constant checks (`1000` → reject, `1024` → accept, [`#L3456-L3457`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/pci.rs#L3456-L3457)) test the validator on every boot rather than the device.
  - Smallest fix: none needed now. If #9's `ginux-kernel-policy` crate lands, `validate_network_queue_size` is a natural pure function to move there, and these constants would become a host unit test.
  - Overengineering risk: **Medium.** Don't build a virtio-geometry test framework or mock device for this. The validator is one line.

### Claims checked and confirmed
- Every virtio-net initialization path already calls `validate_network_queue_size` before programming `QUEUE_SIZE` ([`pci.rs#L1236`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/pci.rs#L1236), [`#L1351`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/pci.rs#L1351), [`#L2254`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/pci.rs#L2254), [`#L2545`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/pci.rs#L2545), [`#L2580`](https://github.com/gmkurtzer/ginux/blob/64effa48538a52d081d77fe79d566675f8323e96/kernel/src/arch/x86_64/pci.rs#L2580)). In the kernel, only the verification check required 256.
- The validator rejects 0, 7, 255 and 1000 and accepts 8, 256 and 1024, and it has no upper-bound problem, since the largest power of two in a `u16` is 32768, the virtio maximum.
- Scope stayed as stated: no change to queue allocation, notification layout or negotiation.
- On QEMU 10.0.13 the kernel-side assertion from #4 is gone with this PR applied (the boot reaches `GINUX_KERNEL_OK`).

Runtime check of this branch on QEMU 10.0.13, since the gate notes it was not run there.

Host: Linux x86-64 (CachyOS 7.2.7), Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, KVM, guests pinned to P-cores.
QEMU 10.0.13 (Debian 1:10.0.13+ds-0+deb13u1), OVMF 2025.02-8+deb13u1, Rust 1.99.0.

- main 22d20a6: `make check` passes. `make test` panics with "virtio network initialization invariant failed" (issue #4 reproduced).
- PR #10 64effa4: the virtio panic is gone. The virtio-net and block IOMMU fault self-tests validate, and the kernel reaches GINUX_KERNEL_OK.

So the fix works at runtime on 10.0.13. `make test` still fails on this host for a separate reason that also affects main and other QEMU versions; details in #14.

One more data point: on QEMU 11.1.2 (Debian trixie-backports), both main and this branch panic with "expected IOMMU fault validation or recovery failed". The VT-d fault record changes from pasid=0xffffffff (10.0.13) to pasid=0x0 (11.1.2), which looks like the same class of version drift as #4.
